2. **Compatibility guard** stops querying a collection with a different embedding model — the hardest silent-failure class in RAG.

# ADR 0001 — Hybrid search is implemented but not the defaultStatus: accepted (2026-10-24)## Context
Dense retrieval misses exact tokens (identifiers, codes); BM25 misses paraphrase. Hybrid retrieval (dense + sparse, reciprocal rank fusion) is the usual remedy.## Decision
Implement hybrid retrieval (`Retrieval:Strategy = Hybrid`, Qdrant sparse vectors with IDF, client-side RRF) and keep **`Dense` the default**.## Evidence
`golden-v1.1.0`, `text-embedding-3-small`. Default settings: document nDCG@10 dense 0.903, hybrid 0.857. After tuning weight, k and candidate count on a tuning split
and validating **once** on a held-out split (protocol committed first): held-out nDCG@10 dense 0.861, tuned hybrid 0.785, difference −0.076, 95 % bootstrap interval
[−0.155, −0.010]; all three pre-registered adoption conditions failed. A synthetic-embedder run had suggested the opposite; it was an artefact of a weak dense leg.

title: ADR 0002 — Query-cache keys carry the index version and the whole retrieval fingerprint
text:
# ADR 0002 — Query-cache keys carry the index version and the whole retrieval fingerprintStatus: accepted (2026-10-24)## Context
The query cache keyed on `collection|topK|filters|query`. Re-indexing a document, changing the embedding model, or two filters whose text collided kept serving stale or wrong results.
Three failing regression tests reproduced it before any fix.## Decision
`CollectionMetadata.IndexVersion` (an opaque token, new on every index run) and a length-prefixed, hashed key over: schema version, collection, index version, embedding provider/model/size,
strategy id (including fusion parameters and, later, reranker identity and candidate budget), topK, filters, query. Invalidation is by key change, not deletion. Degraded results are never cached.## Consequences
No distributed delete races; old entries expire by TTL. GUID tokens rather than counters because Qdrant has no atomic increment. A read/write race can only mis-serve one answer, not pin it.
Details and failure modes: knowledge base chapter 8.
